html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. API: application programming interface; SDK: software development kit; MCP: Model Context Protocol

  • How Claude interprets instructions across interfaces: Claude Code, Desktop, claude.ai, the API and SDKs
  • Content boundaries, schema design, session hygiene and plugin management
  • Configuration management: CLAUDE.md, settings.json, model version pinning, prompt versioning and plugin dependencies

2Claude Application Design

Running case

Tidewater's Prompt Behaves Differently

  • A developer tests the claims prompt in the claude.ai chat and it works well
  • The same text pasted into the API gives a different style and misses a rule
  • In Claude Code a teammate gets yet another answer

The same words, different interfaces

Interface Who supplies the instructions and tools
API / client SDKs You: the system prompt, the history, the tools. Nothing else is added
claude.ai and Desktop Anthropic adds product instructions, features and optional project or user preferences
Claude Code Anthropic's coding system prompt plus your CLAUDE.md, rules, skills, settings and tools
Agent SDK The agent loop and built-in tools of Claude Code as a library, configured in your code
  • Test in the interface you ship. A prompt tuned in a chat app is not automatically right for the API, because the chat app adds its own context.
  • Instructions do not travel between interfaces: project instructions in claude.ai, a system prompt in the API and CLAUDE.md in Claude Code are separate places.

Content boundaries and schemas

  • Separate instructions from data. Put rules in the system prompt and wrap documents and user text in clear tags, so the model knows what is data and what is an instruction (Module 13).
  • Set boundaries for what the assistant should do and refuse (scope, PII handling, no legal advice) and say how to refuse.
  • Schema design (for tools and structured output): clear descriptions, required versus optional fields, enums for fixed sets, nullable fields when data may be missing, and a version for schemas that other systems consume.

Session hygiene

Practice Why
One task per session Unrelated history is noise and can mislead
Start fresh (or clear) when switching tasks Stale context causes drift
Compact or summarize long sessions Keeps context lean (Module 9)
Do not leave secrets or private data in a shared session Avoids leakage

Plugin management

  • A plugin packages skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers as one unit installed from a marketplace; it has a manifest (.claude-plugin/plugin.json).
  • Manage plugins deliberately: install only trusted sources, review what a plugin adds (it can run hooks and tools), enable it per project, and remember each plugin adds context cost.
Exam tip

"Works in the chat app, differs in the API" → the interfaces supply different instructions and context; recreate the needed instructions in the API request.

3Configuration Management

Item What to know
CLAUDE.md Persistent instructions for Claude Code: user, project (shared) and directory levels; commit the project file
settings.json User ~/.claude/settings.json (all your projects); shared project .claude/settings.json (commit it: team permissions, hooks, plugins, env); project local .claude/settings.local.json (kept out of git); managed settings from the organization
Model version pinning Use the full model ID (for example claude-sonnet-5-5) instead of an alias that moves; in Claude Code use the full name or ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL variables. Current model IDs are pinned snapshots
Prompt versioning Keep prompts in files under version control, give them a version, record changes, test with evals, roll back if quality drops
Plugin dependencies Record plugin sources and versions, and update on purpose, because a plugin update changes behavior
  • Why pin: an alias or "latest" can change behavior without a code change, and your evals stop being comparable. Pin, then upgrade on purpose after running evals.
  • Shared versus personal: put team rules in the committed project file; keep personal overrides in the local file or the user file.

[Verify live] Claude Code model aliases (opus, sonnet, haiku, fable, best, opusplan) follow the newest version for your provider and update over time; to pin, use the full model name or the matching environment variable. As of 8 November 2026.

Exam tip

Reproducible behavior needs a pinned model, a versioned prompt and a committed settings file; "latest" and personal settings break reproducibility.

Exam tip

Prompts, schemas and settings are code: commit them, review them, test them with evals and roll them back when quality drops.

4Exam Q&A

S1A prompt works in the claude.ai chat but behaves differently through the API. What is the most likely reason?

  • AThe model is a different size
  • BThe API ignores system prompts
  • CThe API uses a different programming language than the chat application does
  • DThe chat app adds its own instructions and context that the API lacks
Show the answer

Answer: D. Interfaces supply different instructions and features; the API contains only what you send.

S2A team wants every developer to get the same permission rules and hooks in Claude Code. Where should they put them?

  • AIn a chat message
  • BIn each developer's own ~/.claude/settings.json on their personal machine
  • CIn .claude/settings.local.json
  • DIn the committed .claude/settings.json of the project
Show the answer

Answer: D. The shared project settings file reaches teammates through version control.

S3A developer wants a personal override for one project that must not be committed. Where does it belong?

  • A.claude/settings.local.json
  • BThe managed settings
  • CCLAUDE.md at the project root
  • D.claude/settings.json
Show the answer

Answer: A. The local settings file applies to you in that project and stays out of git.

S4An application relies on a moving model alias instead of a full model ID, and its answers drift after the alias moves to a newer version. What is the best practice?

  • ALeave the alias and add more prompt text
  • BSwitch aliases daily
  • CPin the full model ID, re-run evals, and upgrade deliberately
  • DDisable evals
Show the answer

Answer: C. A pinned ID keeps behavior reproducible until you choose to upgrade.

S5Where should the claims prompt live so changes are reviewable and reversible?

  • AIn the model's weights
  • BIn a versioned file in git, tested by evals before every release
  • COnly inside the production database, edited live whenever someone has a better idea
  • DIn a developer's notes app
Show the answer

Answer: B. Prompts are code: version, review, test and roll back.

S6Which describes good session hygiene?

  • AOne long session that is reused for every task during the whole week
  • BPasting the whole repository into every session
  • CNever clearing context
  • DA fresh session per task, compacting long ones, and no secrets in shared sessions
Show the answer

Answer: D. Focused sessions, with compaction for long ones, avoid stale and misleading context in the window.

S7A team installs a plugin from an unknown source because it looks useful. What is the concern?

  • APlugins only change the colors of the terminal and nothing else about behavior
  • BPlugins are always read-only
  • CPlugins cannot be disabled
  • DA plugin can add hooks, tools and MCP servers, so untrusted ones are risky
Show the answer

Answer: D. Plugins package executable components; install trusted sources and review what they add.

S8A schema for claim data will be used by three other systems. What should the developer do?

  • AChange field names whenever convenient, as long as the producing application still runs correctly
  • BUse clear descriptions, required and optional fields, enums, nullable fields and a version
  • CKeep the schema undocumented
  • DMake every field free text
Show the answer

Answer: B. Systems that consume the data need a stable, documented and versioned contract so changes do not break them.

S9Which TWO belong in the committed project configuration of a Claude Code repository? Select TWO.

  • ALocal overrides that only one engineer needs
  • BEach person's private experiments
  • CA developer's personal API key
  • DShared project instructions in CLAUDE.md
  • ETeam permission rules and hooks in .claude/settings.json
Show the answer

Answer: D, E. Shared settings and instructions are committed; keys and personal overrides are not.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Interfaces API = only what you send; apps and Claude Code add their own instructions and features; test in the interface you ship
Boundaries Rules in system; data tagged; say how to refuse; PII scope
Schemas Descriptions, required/optional, enums, nullable, version
Session hygiene One task per session, fresh start, compact, no secrets in shared sessions
Plugins Skills + agents + hooks + MCP in one unit; trusted sources; context cost; per-project
settings.json User · shared project (commit) · project local (not committed) · managed
Pinning Full model ID (pinned snapshot) or ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL; aliases move
Prompt versioning Files in git, version, evals, rollback
